_comment: RS2 Local — single source of truth for paths + pipeline settings. All paths absolute (Windows).
_ctx_note: Real payload = RS2.txt(~5.2k tok) + fed data(~4k tok) + accumulating prior stages. 16384 overflows late stages, so both run at 24576 (fits w/ generation headroom; ~96% GPU, 4% CPU spill). The 16384/100%-GPU figure applied only to the old manual-data flow.
_seed_note: Deterministic sampling base, added 2026-08-20. Every LLM call now derives its seed as sha256(seed_base|ticker|site|index) -> 31-bit int (run_rs2.call_seed), recorded per run in reports/{T}_{ts}/run_meta.json. Same seed_base + same inputs -> byte-identical draws (proven on rs2-analyst-deep at ctx 65536; production windows proven by test T1). Distinct per-sample indices keep regime's 3-vote majority and the audit's resamples genuine votes. Retries perturb deterministically (attempt 0 always sends the exact derived seed). Change seed_base to draw a fresh but still-reproducible universe. NOT forwarded to the --api cloud backend: api_chat sends no seed and cloud results remain unreproducible - run_meta.json records api_mode so those runs are labelled.
_watchdog_note: orchestrate.py kills a single run_rs2 child (and unloads both models) if it exceeds this many minutes, then marks the name failed + retries it (orchestrate.py:49 MAX_RETRIES=3). CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (the old note's '~11 min/name, 3.5x headroom' was pre-migration). MEASURED over reports/_orchestrate.log (57,723 lines): the watchdog has fired exactly 4 times ever — NOVT x1, and ARGX x3 on 2026-08-18 (13:07:54 / 13:54:28 / 14:38:02), which BURNED THE FULL RETRY BUDGET AND NEVER PUBLISHED: ARGX's newest bundle is still reports/ARGX_20260723_011459. Attempt 3 shows the cause — deep research alone took 1,967s (32.8 min) across four subqueries (1035s / 775s / 98s / 59s via searxng), leaving ~7 min of the 40 for six analyst stages that need ~10. So the binding constraint is NOT analyst generation, it is deep_research latency. STRUCTURAL GAP (unfixed, needs an operator decision): run_rs2.py:2038 calls subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, ...) with NO timeout=, and deep_research.py contains exactly one timeout in the whole file (line 161, a 20s SearXNG preflight probe). The research phase is therefore unbounded, and this ticker-level watchdog is the only thing bounding it. capture_output also buffers the child until exit, so the log shows total silence during research and cannot distinguish a stall from slow-but-healthy work. RAISING THIS NUMBER WEAKENS THE ONLY BOUND ON THE UNBOUNDED PHASE — bound deep_research at source instead. Override per-run with --ticker-timeout-min.
_regime_note: MRI current_regime.json can be synthetic_sample (future-dated). rs2_data.py only uses its regime probabilities when the file date is within regime_max_age_days of today; otherwise it feeds real macro_state.json and lets the model classify.
_research_note: Deep-research (LDR) runs in research-venv on a CLEAN model (NOT rs2-analyst — its baked RS2 prompt would contaminate LDR's research prompts). Tavily primary w/ quota guard -> SearXNG fallback (local/unlimited). snippets_only=False = read full pages.
_research_timeout_note: HARD CEILING on the deep-research phase, added 2026-08-20. Until now this was the only UNBOUNDED step in the pipeline: run_rs2.run_research called subprocess.run with no timeout= and deep_research.py contains exactly one timeout in the whole file (line 161, a 20s SearXNG preflight probe). The 40-minute ticker watchdog in orchestrate.py was the only thing bounding it, which is why raising ticker_timeout_min would have WEAKENED the only bound on the only unbounded phase. SIZED FROM MEASUREMENT over 3,437 logged subquery completions in reports/_orchestrate.log: a per-ticker research phase runs p50 320s (5.3 min), p90 390s, p95 478s, p99 525s (8.8 min). 900s is 1.7x the p99 and 2.8x the median. Exactly ONE phase of 252 on record exceeds it - ARGX on 2026-08-18 at 1,967s (32.8 min), driven by a single searxng subquery that took 1,035s against a p90 of 121s. That run was killed by the 40-minute watchdog anyway, three times, and ARGX has not published since 2026-07-23. So this ceiling costs nothing measured and converts a silent 40-minute hang into a loud 15-minute failure that names its cause. On timeout the child is killed TREE-AND-ALL (taskkill /T /F - the LDR child spawns grandchildren, so Popen.kill would orphan them), the research model's VRAM is released, and the ticker exits 3, the same path as a research infra error: we do not analyse on a brief we could not build.
_vram_note: rs2-analyst and rs2-research are BOTH ~23GB on a 24GB card, so they can never co-reside. The unload is a VERIFIED barrier (ops.wait_unloaded): after keep_alive:0 it polls /api/ps AND nvidia-smi free VRAM until the release is observed, because ollama's 200 only means the request finished — it tears the llama-server subprocess down asynchronously. The old blind time.sleep(2) lost that race and OOM'd the next load. free_required is the floor the next ~23GB load needs; timeout is a hard failure (ticker aborts + Telegram) rather than loading into a half-freed card.
_stage_ctx_note: Raised 24576 -> 49152 on 2026-08-20. CORRECTED 2026-08-20: the original note's stated cause did not happen. Re-measured over the three Ollama server logs (2,821 'stop processing' lines): 226 completions hit a context wall, bucketed by n_tokens = num_ctx-1 — 177 at 24575 (the old stage window; 08-17 x63, 08-18 x105, 08-19 x9), 45 at 32767, 2 at 8191, 1 at 40959, 1 at 65535. What overflowed was prompt PLUS generation, not the prompt alone; the earlier '26' was a single-log, single-bucket count. The decision to raise stage_ctx stands; the reason recorded for it did not. *** OPEN AND UNADDRESSED: 45 of those truncations are at 32767 = final_ctx-1, and final_ctx is STILL 32768. The session fixed the stage window and left the final window alone. Since 9ba2929 made done_reason=='length' raise, a final-assembly truncation is no longer a silently-published stub — run_rs2.py:2156 passes retries=1, so `for attempt in range(1)` runs ONE attempt with no context escalation, the RuntimeError is unwrapped, and the ticker dies outright and burns a full rerun including deep research. 45 events fell on 2026-08-17/18 alone. This will fire on the first sweep after resume, preferentially on the longest reports. *** Also still unmeasured in both directions: what a stage actually GENERATES at 49,152 with thinking off. rs2-analyst has never run a production sweep at this window.
_final_ctx_note: Raised 32768 -> 49152 on 2026-08-20 (operator decision). MEASURED CAUSE: 45 completions ended at exactly n_tokens=32767 = the old final_ctx-1 across 2026-08-17/18 in the Ollama server logs — the final report hitting the wall mid-sentence. That used to publish as a silent stub; since 9ba2929 run_rs2.py:236 raises on done_reason=='length', and run_rs2.py:2154 passes retries=1, so the loop makes ONE attempt, the context-escalation ladder never advances past attempt 0, and the RuntimeError is unwrapped — the ticker dies and burns a full rerun including deep research against MAX_RETRIES=3. Two consumers, both gain headroom: the final assembly (:2154) and the tier-2 auditor (:1783, whose pack is ~45KB / 13-14K tokens per the comment at :1711). SIDE BENEFIT: stage_ctx is also 49152, so the stages and the final assembly no longer differ in window size — that removes a context-size reload mid-ticker (the failure mode the retry comment at :204 calls out as a source of transient Ollama 500s). STILL OPEN: retries=1 at :2154 means a report that overruns even 49,152 still dies with no second attempt. The operator chose the ceiling raise alone; the retry option was declined, so that tail remains uncovered and should be watched on the first sweep after resume.
_depth_note: DEPTH-TIER REPLACEMENT PIPELINE (operator-accepted spec 2026-08-21; production dropped). depth_pipeline.py per ticker: research (cache-aware, research_timeout_s bound) -> depth_samples seeded runs with tools -> plausibility guard -> BAND-DIRECTION verdict (price above whole IV band = overvalued, below = undervalued, inside = hold; spread -> size hint, never pass/fail). orchestrate_depth.py sweeps the live book, one child at a time, watchdogged at depth_ticker_timeout_min with tree-kill + unload. Verdicts append to cache/depth_ledger.jsonl; newest-per-ticker rebuilt into cache/depth_overlay.json — LOCAL ONLY, the site switches over by operator action, never by code. The frozen llm_overlay.json is a failure record and is never touched.
_depth_cadence_note: CADENCE (operator-approved 2026-08-21). Daily direction refresh = screener-side price vs stored band (free). Model re-runs are TRIGGER-DRIVEN via depth_triggers.py, all detectors deterministic: 8-K filed after the verdict (SanDisk-class news), 10-Q/10-K filed (quarterly baseline), price moved > depth_move_trigger_pct since the verdict, or verdict older than depth_rotation_days. Priority: triggered first, then never-analysed baseline, then rotation - rotation only runs when no triggered work remains. SEC submissions cached daily per CIK in cache/sec_submissions/. Red button: cache/DEPTH_PAUSED (cache/PAUSED stays forever to hold the dropped pipeline's scheduled task down).
